howItWorks: Choose the type of QR code — a link, UPI payment, WhatsApp chat, Wi-Fi login and more — and fill in the fields that appear.
Your QR code updates instantly as you type; adjust the size, error correction and color if you like.
Press Download PNG for sharing on screen, or Download SVG for sharp printing at any size.
examples: Put a UPI QR code on your shop counter so customers can pay you straight from their phone.
Print a Wi-Fi QR code for guests so they can join without typing the password.
Add a WhatsApp QR code to a poster or visiting card that opens a chat with a ready message.

faq.q: Is my information sent to a server?
faq.a: No. The QR code is generated in your browser, so the links, Wi-Fi passwords and payment details you enter are never uploaded or stored.

faq.q: Do these QR codes expire or track scans?
faq.a: No. These are static QR codes: the data is stored inside the code itself, so it never expires and there is no tracking or redirect service in between.

faq.q: Which error correction level should I choose?
faq.a: Medium is a good default. Choose High if the code will be printed on something that may get scuffed or if you want to place a logo over the centre. Lower levels give simpler, easier-to-scan codes for short text.

faq.q: Can I use the UPI QR code to receive payments?
faq.a: Yes. Enter your UPI ID and, optionally, an amount and note. Scanning opens the payer’s UPI app with the details pre-filled. Always scan your own code with a payment app before printing it.

faq.q: Should I download PNG or SVG?
faq.a: Use PNG for websites, chats and social posts. Use SVG for print: it is a vector file that stays perfectly sharp at any size, from a business card to a banner.
